subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the repository-owned glob compatibility contract and event-loop interleaving between bootstrap hook handlers introduced by this PR?
rationale: Tests and benchmark proof support the performance fix, but CI cannot decide whether these compatibility and session-scheduling changes are acceptable permanent runtime contracts.

options.title: Accept after refresh
options.body: Refresh the branch, rerun exact-head validation, and merge with the current parity tests and internal-only API boundary as the maintained contract.

options.title: Narrow hook scheduling
options.body: Keep the asynchronous file and glob work but defer yielding between hook handlers if shared-context interleaving is not an acceptable runtime contract.

options.title: Reject custom traversal
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue a different cooperative glob mechanism if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own glob semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept after refresh
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, rerun exact-head validation, and merge with the current parity tests and internal-only API boundary as the maintained contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work spans the workspace bootstrap cache and embedded-run preparation boundaries affected by the decision.
